limitations: Download-count and GitHub-star figures vary somewhat across third-party trackers (Socket.dev vs Snyk vs npmjs.com) for the same package and week; figures are reported as retrieved rather than reconciled to a single canonical source.

This shard covers only the TypeScript language column; cross-language comparability of these same domains/scores is established by the runner from sibling per-language shards using the same predeclared domain list and selection rule where applicable.

metric.package_ecosystem_activity_mainte.score_rationale: Sampled flagship packages across validation, testing, type-definitions, and core tooling show release activity within the last 1-7 days to 3 months, with independent third-party health scorers (Snyk, Socket.dev, PkgPulse) classifying maintenance as 'Sustainable' or 'Healthy'/'very good'. One sampled flagship (Express core framework) showed a materially slower 9-month release gap, which is reflected as a partial deduction since package_ecosystem_activity_maintenance must account for variance, not only the most-active samples. The registry-wide caveat that raw package counts include abandoned packages was also treated as a moderating factor rather than a straightforward positive.

signals_examined.signal: Snyk's maintenance analysis found zod demonstrates a positive version release cadence with at least one new version released in the past 3 months, and scored its maintenance status as Sustainable; the GitHub releases page shows dated commits and version bumps within the prior week of the snapshot.

npmjs.com listed Jest's latest version (30.5.2) as published a day before the snapshot, and pkgpulse's health-score comparison rated Jest 86/100 for combined maintenance, quality, security and popularity signals.

@types/node's npm listing showed a last-updated timestamp 3 days before the snapshot with 320,990,123 downloads, reflecting a large, continuously-refreshed community type-maintenance pipeline behind DefinitelyTyped.
The npm CLI's stable release was recorded as version 12.0.2 on 29 July 2026, indicating an actively maintained core toolchain component roughly two months before the snapshot.

Express's latest version (5.2.1) was listed as published 9 months before the snapshot, a slower cadence than the other sampled packages, though the framework is still the production-recommended release per its Technical Committee and remains widely deployed.

The public npm registry replication endpoint reported roughly 4.04 million registry documents as of mid-2026, described as a registry-scale indicator that includes abandoned and deprecated as well as actively maintained packages, a caveat applied when interpreting raw registry size as an activity signal.

domains_examined.finding: Express sits behind an estimated 1.2 million production websites and ships tens of millions of weekly npm downloads; npmjs.com lists 107,905 other projects in the registry depending on it, with a maintained 5.x line (latest 5.2.1).

React's weekly npm downloads were measured at roughly 126.6-142 million in mid-2026 reporting, with 230,000+ GitHub stars, dwarfing the next largest framework by a wide margin; official React docs and tooling (create-react-app successors, Vite templates) ship first-class TypeScript support.

Zod receives on the order of 200-275 million weekly npm downloads across independent trackers (Socket.dev and Snyk), is described as a TypeScript-first schema declaration and validation library with static type inference, and its maintenance status was scored 'Sustainable' with a positive release cadence.

Jest receives about 45.5 million weekly downloads, carries an overall package-health score of 86/100 rated 'very good' with strong maintenance and popularity components, and its latest release (30.5.2) was published a day before the snapshot.

domains_examined.candidate_universe: redux/@reduxjs/toolkit, mobx, immer, immutable, recoil, zustand, jotai
domains_examined.finding: Redux Toolkit is reported as remaining the standard for large-scale React applications requiring strict unidirectional data flow, with approximately 9 million weekly downloads, alongside actively growing alternatives (Zustand ~7M monthly, Jotai, Recoil) in the same category.

domains_examined.domain: Type-definition safety net for untyped packages
domains_examined.finding: DefinitelyTyped is described as the largest repository of TypeScript type definitions in the world, containing community-maintained type definitions for over 8,000 npm packages that do not ship their own types, automatically published to the @types npm scope; @types/node alone shows 320,990,123 downloads with its most recent update 3 days before the snapshot.

The public npm registry replication endpoint reported about 4.04 million registry documents in mid-2026, and npm is described as remaining one of the most widely used software package registries, serving billions of downloads on a regular basis.

metric.third_party_library_availability_.score_rationale: All 7 predeclared domains have a mature, high-download, actively-shipping flagship library with either native TypeScript-first design (Zod) or first-class/official TypeScript type support (Express, React, Jest, Redux Toolkit), plus a dedicated large-scale community safety net (DefinitelyTyped, 8,000+ typed packages) for anything not natively typed. Coverage is judged near-complete but not scored 100 because a small residual of niche/enterprise domains still rely on community (not maintainer-shipped) types of variable quality, per DefinitelyTyped's own scope note that untyped packages are common in the broader npm ecosystem.

predeclared_sampling.candidate_universe_source: https://www.npmcharts.com/ fixed comparison-category groupings, snapshot week of September 14-20, 2026
predeclared_sampling.note_on_raw_popularity_proxies: Weekly download counts and GitHub star counts are used only as declared, cross-checked supporting evidence within these metrics, not as a standalone proxy. Limitation: npm download counts include CI/CD reinstall noise and do not equal unique human users.
predeclared_sampling.retrieval_route: npmjs.com package pages, socket.dev / security.snyk.io package-health reports, npmcharts.com, and one Wikipedia cross-check per domain; identical retrieval depth (one search pass, top official/registry sources) applied per domain
predeclared_sampling.selection_rule: For each domain, the single package with the highest weekly npm downloads / most explicit ecosystem-standard status among the fixed candidate list published by npmcharts.com (a language-neutral third-party npm comparison tool) was selected before evidence was collected. npmcharts.com groups npm packages into fixed comparison categories (web server frameworks, ORM/DB clients, CSS-in-JS, frontend frameworks, build/lint/test tooling, state management, logging, UI component kits, meta-frameworks, utilities, bundlers), giving a reproducible, benchmark-independent candidate universe.
